_comment: v3.66.1227 row-216 battery. The census now asks the VALIDATED reader instead of counting pathnames, so the mutants are the ways that could quietly become a pathname count again, or could over-correct into calling everything UNKNOWN. M5 is the over-correction: a census that reports UNKNOWN for a perfectly readable registry passes every test about malformed finals and is useless. FIRST RUN: 4 caught, M3 ESCAPED -- nothing drove the parser off its happy path, so the fallback could be replaced with a guessed count and stay green. test_bd_fleet_refuses_to_guess_when_bd_jobs_output_does_not_parse was added for it.
subject: v3.66.1227 -- bd-fleet counts validated jobs, not pathnames

mutants.label: M1 count pathnames again instead of asking the validated reader
mutants.new: jobs_out="$(ls /tmp/bd-jobs/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l) live, 0 stale on x"

mutants.label: M2 fold malformed finals back into the valid count
M3 an unparseable summary guesses a number instead of UNKNOWN
M4 an UNREADABLE registry is described as an EMPTY one again
M5 every registry is graded UNKNOWN, which passes the malformed tests and is useless
